meta.scope: US national environment and campaign messaging for the Nov 3, 2026 midterms. Individual Senate/House/governor race polls deliberately excluded.
meta.rules: Every number appears in the cited source (fetched page or search-result title/snippet). 'not found' means not located in accessible sources. Values tagged 'computed' are arithmetic on sourced numbers. Party messages are paraphrased in each side's own terms, without endorsement or rebuttal.
gaps: Web-search budget ran out mid-research, so these could not be retrieved: current Economist, Split Ticket, RacetotheWH, Strength In Numbers and CNalysis forecasts; AdImpact ad-theme breakdowns by party; committee press releases (DSCC, DCCC, NRSC, NRCC).
The NYT, Economist and BLS CPI pages were blocked or required permission. Values for those come from secondary sources, cited.

rates_debt.item: Treasury note yield reached a 19-year high of 5.104%

tariffs_and_prices.item: The temporary 10% Section 122 global surcharge (in place since Feb 24, after the Supreme Court struck down the IEEPA tariffs) expired. Section 301 tariffs of 10% or 12.5% on 60 economies (99.4% of imports) replaced it, with the EU and Taiwan capped at 10% combined.
Brazil: an additional 25% Section 301 tariff, for 37.5% in total, with exemptions

50% tariff on specified Canadian goods under Section 338, announced Jul 20. Law-firm alert gives Aug 19; Wikipedia gives Aug 22 and about $28B of goods. Canada retaliated on about $20B of US goods (Aug 25) and raised steel/aluminum tariffs to 50% (Sep 8).
Trump announced a 20% fee on cargo through the Strait of Hormuz and a reinstated blockade of Iranian ports
IEEPA tariff refunds are being processed, most within 60-90 days after a CAPE declaration is accepted

events.event: The US-Iran ceasefire deal (Islamabad Memorandum, Jun 17) collapsed after Iran attacked commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz
events.why_it_matters: Restarted the war that began Feb 28. Energy prices and the war became central campaign topics.

events.event: Trump announced a 20% fee on Hormuz cargo and a blockade of Iranian ports from Jul 14
events.why_it_matters: Escalation affecting shipping and energy markets

events.event: In a national address, Trump repeated claims of fraud in the 2020 election
events.why_it_matters: Election-integrity theme ahead of the midterms

events.event: Major disaster declaration approved for Texas flooding in more than 28 counties
events.why_it_matters: Disaster response, amid the FEMA staffing disputes later ruled on in court (Sep 12)

events.event: Trump announced 50% tariffs on Canadian goods under Section 338, effective Aug 19-22. Canada suspended trade talks (Aug 21) and retaliated (Aug 25).
events.why_it_matters: Trade and prices; trade approval later hit an all-time low (Silver Bulletin)

events.event: House passed a stopgap (H.R. 9770) 220-205 to extend FY2026 funding to Dec 4
events.why_it_matters: First attempt to avoid a fourth shutdown of the term before the election

events.event: Trump attended the dignified transfer at Dover of US soldiers killed in Iranian strikes
events.why_it_matters: US casualties from the war

events.event: Section 122 tariffs expired; the global tariff regime was rebuilt under Section 301 (10%-12.5% on 60 economies)
events.why_it_matters: Kept broad tariffs in place after the Supreme Court's IEEPA ruling

events.event: Advance estimate: Q2 GDP growth slowed to 1.5%, later revised to 2.2% on Sep 30
events.why_it_matters: Economic backdrop

events.event: Trump Media announced a paid 'Trump API' giving businesses early access to Trump's posts; critics called it corruption
events.why_it_matters: Feeds the Democratic 'corruption' message

events.event: Senate passed a bipartisan stopgap funding bill
events.why_it_matters: Set up the September House vote that averted a shutdown

events.event: Todd Blanche sworn in as Attorney General; Trump signed an executive order reducing recommended childhood vaccines
events.why_it_matters: Personnel turnover; vaccine policy drew criticism as measles reached a 35-year high, including from GOP Sen. Cassidy (Sep 16)

events.event: Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt announced her resignation, effective end of August
events.why_it_matters: White House communications turnover before the fall campaign

events.event: Trump told Americans to accept higher gas prices as the cost of stopping Iran's nuclear program
events.why_it_matters: Puts the administration's national-security framing directly against cost-of-living concerns

events.event: Two dozen states and DC sued to block Trump's executive order restricting mail voting for the midterms
events.why_it_matters: Election-rules fight; a federal judge blocked USPS implementation on Sep 13

events.event: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh warned at Jackson Hole of elevated inflation and interest rates
events.why_it_matters: Signaled the September rate hike

events.event: Supreme Court allowed White House ballroom construction to continue, 5-4
events.why_it_matters: About two-thirds of Americans rate such projects a low priority (Reuters/Ipsos)

events.event: House passed the stopgap 370-48 (funding through Dec 11), and Trump signed it Sep 2. The House also passed a non-binding resolution denouncing socialism, 220-192.
events.why_it_matters: No pre-election shutdown; full-year FY2027 bills pushed to a post-election December deadline. The term had already seen three partial shutdowns totaling a record 161 days.

events.event: Diesel hit a record $5.85/gal national average. The White House confirmed Melania Trump would skip the GOP midterm convention, as would at least 45 GOP lawmakers.
events.why_it_matters: Fuel costs; some Republicans keeping distance from a Trump-centered event

events.event: Missouri map in limbo: Justice Kavanaugh declined to intervene, a federal judge ordered the GOP map used, and the state Supreme Court had blocked it pending a referendum
events.why_it_matters: Part of the mid-decade redistricting fights (TX, CA, FL, MO, OH, NC, LA, TN, AL, UT) shaping the House map

events.event: At the two-day GOP midterm convention in Dallas, Trump proposed a $5,000 payment to every adult if Republicans win both chambers (estimated cost $1.3T). The same day, the WSJ reported advisers privately warned the Iran war could last through 2029, and the administration proposed a 2030 census citizenship question.
events.why_it_matters: Centerpiece of the Republican closing pitch. Reuters/Ipsos found 63% disapproved of the payment offer.

events.event: August CPI: 3.4% y/y headline, 2.4% core
events.why_it_matters: Inflation was the top issue and Trump's weakest issue rating

events.event: Fed raised rates 25bp to 3.75%-4.00%, its first hike since 2023. The House also passed a resolution requiring Trump to end the Iran war, its third such passage.
events.why_it_matters: Borrowing costs rising into the election; congressional pressure over the war

events.event: Reuters/Ipsos: Trump approval at 32%, his career low in that poll (fielded Sep 17-20)
events.why_it_matters: Marks the late-September slide in averages

events.event: Michigan GOP Senate nominee Mike Rogers and Sen. Jon Husted (R-OH) called for an end to the Iran war
events.why_it_matters: Some vulnerable Republicans breaking with the White House on the war

events.event: VP Vance and CMS announced plans to remove 760,000 ACA enrollees over alleged fraud
events.why_it_matters: Health care is Democrats' strongest trust issue (D+24, NYT/Siena); the administration frames the move as anti-fraud

events.event: Democratic groups sued over alleged plans to deploy armed federal agents to polling sites
events.why_it_matters: Election-administration conflict heading into November

events.event: Trump rejected an Iranian ceasefire proposal and reportedly told aides he expects to resume bombing after the midterms. The Supreme Court allowed an expanded citizenship database for voter-roll review.
events.why_it_matters: The war stays live through Election Day; voter-roll policy cleared to proceed

events.event: FY2027 began without a shutdown. AAA reported a record September gas average of $4.33.
events.why_it_matters: Gas prices are a top concern; Democrats lead on 'gas prices' 40-27 (NPR/Marist)

events.event: September jobs report: +29,000 payrolls, unemployment 4.2%
events.why_it_matters: Labor market softening alongside higher inflation

events.event: Silver Bulletin net approval hit an all-time low of -23.5
events.why_it_matters: National-environment low point; it was -21.9 on Oct 9

events.event: Pew: Trump approval 30%, and Democrats lead Republicans by 17 on 'extremely motivated' to vote
events.why_it_matters: Enthusiasm gap favoring Democrats, the reverse of October 2022

events.event: UMich preliminary sentiment fell to 46.3; one-year inflation expectations rose to 4.7%
events.why_it_matters: Consumer pessimism

dem.detail: DNC (spokesperson Kendall Witmer, Oct 9): Democrats will 'focus on lowering costs.' She argued that Trump's record-low approval, rising gas and grocery prices, and the Iran conflict are hurting Republicans. A Sep 28 Hill op-ed by Schoen and Cooperman describes the Democratic emphasis as 'affordability, competence and checks on Trump.'
DNC pledges to make health care affordable. Health care is the issue where voters trust Democrats most: 60-36 in NYT/Siena.
DNC lists corruption as a focus. Related: on Sep 24, Sens. Warren and Blumenthal pressed AG Blanche over the dismissal of the Adani case.
Op-ed observers describe 'checks on Trump' as a core frame. 44% of voters say their House vote is against Trump and 19% for him (Pew); 45% against (NPR/Marist).

dem.theme: End the Iran war / war costs
dem.detail: The House passed a resolution requiring Trump to end the Iran war for the third time (Sep 16). DNC cites 'the Iran conflict' as hurting Republicans.

24 states and DC sued over the mail-voting executive order (Aug 26), and Democratic groups sued over alleged plans for armed federal agents at polls (Sep 24). Democratic officials call the federal election investigations efforts to intimidate officials and voters.

Fall reservations per AdImpact (June): WinSenate $140M+ across eight Senate seats; House Majority PAC $192M for House races. Senate Majority PAC 'stockpiles record sum' (NYT headline, Jul 10, via Wikipedia).
not found (committee sites not reachable after the search budget ran out)

rep.theme: White House: nationalize the midterms around Trump
rep.detail: Political Wire headline (Sep 2): 'The White House moves to make midterms about Trump' (body not retrieved). Trump headlined a two-day Republican midterm convention in Dallas (Sep 9-10). RNC Chair Joe Gruters called it 'Trump-a-Palooza.'

rep.theme: A $5,000 payment if the GOP holds both chambers
rep.detail: Trump proposed $5,000 for every adult if Republicans win the House and Senate, estimated at $1.3 trillion (Sep 9). Reuters/Ipsos: 63% disapproved.
The House GOP passed a resolution denouncing socialism, 220-192 (Sep 1). The Sep 28 Hill op-ed says Republicans portray Democratic nominees as extreme.
Speaker Johnson blamed Democrats for the 120-day shutdown this Congress, which stemmed from disputes over immigration-enforcement limits (Fox, Sep 3).

Trump asked Americans to accept higher gas prices as the cost of stopping Iran's nuclear program (Aug 14) and rejected an Iranian ceasefire proposal (Sep 25). Some GOP candidates (Rogers, Husted) diverged and called for ending the war.

Mail-voting executive order, an expanded citizenship database for voter-roll review (allowed by SCOTUS Sep 25), a proposed 2030 census citizenship question (Sep 9), and Trump's Jul 16 national address on 2020 fraud claims.
Vance and CMS plan to remove 760,000 ACA enrollees over alleged fraud (Sep 22).
RNC (Apr 2026): special elections 'are special and not a true depiction' of the fall; 'a snapshot of local quirks.'

Senate Leadership Fund plans about $342-350M across eight states, ads airing from early September: $236M defending five GOP seats and $106M targeting three Democratic seats. Largest buys: OH $79M, NC $71M, MI $45M, GA $44M, ME $42M. AdImpact fall reservations: SLF $200M+; Congressional Leadership Fund $144M for the House. Republicans spent nearly $100M on ads in newly drawn districts (Punchbowl/AdImpact via Newsweek, Oct 9).

groups.finding: NYT/Siena (Sep 8-13): 27% approve of Trump; generic ballot D 57, R 34. Economist/YouGov (Aug 7-10): 18% approve, 71% disapprove. Democrats lead independents by 29 (Emerson) and 25 (Marist). About half say their vote is against Trump (Marist). 66% say wrong track (Noble, Aug).

Pew generic ballot: D 51, R 24. Economist/YouGov Trump approval among Hispanic Americans: 27% (Aug 7-10), down from 37% (Jul 17-20). Pew: 57% of Hispanic Trump 2024 voters approve, vs 69% of White Trump voters; Pew calls Hispanic and younger Trump voters the starkest declines.
